problem: "advanced injection raises NOx" can be misread as "improved injection". The meaning is advancing the injection timing, which is the opposite of retarding it to cut NOx.
fix: "advancing the injection timing (starting injection earlier) raises NOx; retarding it lowers NOx but costs fuel economy and power."

problem: "less friction can raise wear" is too compressed. A student may not see why less friction would ever be harmful.
fix: "cutting friction with a thinner oil or a lighter part can raise wear or noise if the oil film or the part strength falls below what the load needs."

problem: The formula is placed right after Miller/Atkinson, so a student may apply it directly to those cycles. Miller/Atkinson efficiency depends on the effective compression ratio, not the geometric one, and the heat-release is not constant volume.
fix: State that ηOtto = 1 − 1/r^(γ−1) is the ideal constant-volume benchmark only; for Miller/Atkinson use the effective compression ratio set by the intake valve closing point. Also note that "a higher compression ratio does the same" means it also raises ideal efficiency.

problem: The cross-reference to 5.8 is plain text, so it is not a clickable chapter link like the other cross-references in the book.
fix: Use a link: "Test procedure and in-cylinder pressure are in 5.8."

problem: Thousands are separated by a space ("26 880 g/h", "22 500 g/h"). Most Indian textbooks use a comma, sometimes the Indian grouping.
fix: Write 26,880 g/h and 22,500 g/h (or keep one style throughout the book).
